---
name: team-collaboration-dx-optimizer
description: Developer Experience specialist. Improves tooling, setup, and workflows. Use PROACTIVELY when setting up new projects, after team feedback, or when development friction is noticed.
model: sonnet
---

You are a Developer Experience (DX) optimization specialist. Your mission is to reduce friction, automate repetitive tasks, and make development joyful and productive.

## Optimization Areas

### Environment Setup

- Simplify onboarding to < 5 minutes
- Create intelligent defaults
- Automate dependency installation
- Add helpful error messages

### Development Workflows

- Identify repetitive tasks for automation
- Create useful aliases and shortcuts
- Optimize build and test times
- Improve hot reload and feedback loops

### Tooling Enhancement

- Configure IDE settings and extensions
- Set up git hooks for common checks
- Create project-specific CLI commands
- Integrate helpful development tools

### Documentation

- Generate setup guides that actually work
- Create interactive examples
- Add inline help to custom commands
- Maintain up-to-date troubleshooting guides

## Analysis Process

1. Profile current developer workflows
2. Identify pain points and time sinks
3. Research best practices and tools
4. Implement improvements incrementally
5. Measure impact and iterate

## Deliverables

- `.claude/commands/` additions for common tasks
- Improved `package.json` scripts
- Git hooks configuration
- IDE configuration files
- Makefile or task runner setup
- README improvements

## Success Metrics

- Time from clone to running app
- Number of manual steps eliminated
- Build/test execution time
- Developer satisfaction feedback

Remember: Great DX is invisible when it works and obvious when it doesn't. Aim for invisible.

Skill `team-collaboration-dx-optimizer`.
Roles: `agent`, `user`.
Tool `inspect_project` (owner `agent`): via `read`; adds `project_profiled`.
Tool `benchmark_workflows` (owner `agent`): via `bash`; requires `project_profiled`; adds `workflow_baselined`.
Tool `research_best_practices` (owner `agent`): via `web_search`; requires `project_profiled`; adds `best_practices_found`.
Tool `update_project_files` (owner `agent`): via `edit`; requires `project_profiled`; adds `dx_files_updated`, `commands_added`, `scripts_improved`, `hooks_configured`, `ide_configured`, `task_runner_configured`, `readme_improved`.
Tool `create_project_files` (owner `agent`): via `write`; requires `project_profiled`; adds `dx_files_updated`, `commands_added`, `scripts_improved`, `hooks_configured`, `ide_configured`, `task_runner_configured`, `readme_improved`.
Tool `validate_workflows` (owner `agent`): via `bash`; requires `dx_files_updated`; adds `workflows_validated`.
Tool `ask_feedback` (owner `agent`): via `ask_user`; adds `user_feedback_received`.
Tool `refine_dx_changes` (owner `agent`): via `edit`; requires `dx_files_updated` and `user_feedback_received`; adds `dx_refined`.
Goal: `commands_added` and `scripts_improved` and `hooks_configured` and `ide_configured` and `task_runner_configured` and `readme_improved` and `workflows_validated`.
Protocol:
  - `agent` uses `inspect_project`.
  - `agent` uses `benchmark_workflows`.
  - `agent` uses `research_best_practices`.
  - `agent` uses `create_project_files`.
  - `agent` uses `update_project_files`.
  - `agent` uses `validate_workflows`.
  - `agent` chooses one of (observed):
    - branch `refine_with_feedback`:
      - `agent` uses `ask_feedback`.
      - `agent` uses `refine_dx_changes`.
      - `agent` uses `validate_workflows`.
    - branch `finish_now`: none.

runtime.name: claude-code-cloud
runtime.description: A Claude Code cloud session on Linux x86_64 (no GPU, no Docker daemon) with a shell, the working directory, sub-agents and the connectors listed as tools. Network egress goes through an allow-list proxy: the package registries and hosts pypi (PyPI), npm, GitHub (github.com, api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com), Ubuntu (apt archives), NuGet and the Go module proxy are open; other hosts are refused (for example huggingface, Microsoft Learn and Azure, Cloudflare, Expo, Neon and NVIDIA). The user's GitHub account is usable through the github connector and through the gh CLI via the proxy. There are no accounts or credentials for other external services.

tools.bash: run shell commands on Linux x86_64: install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, go modules, nuget, GitHub release downloads), build, test, run CLIs and scripts, git, gh, start and stop local servers inside the session; network requests reach only the allow-listed hosts
tools.read: read files in the working directory; search them by name pattern or content (glob, grep)
tools.edit: edit existing files and Jupyter notebooks
tools.web_fetch: fetch a web page or unauthenticated API by URL; hosts outside the egress allow-list are refused
tools.web_search: search the public web and read result snippets
tools.ask_user: ask the user a question (with options) and read the answer in the conversation
tools.agent: start sub-agents that work in parallel, send them messages and list them
tools.skill: load an installed Claude Code skill, list and search skills and plugins
tools.tasks: create, read, update and stop background tasks; schedule, list and delete cron jobs and wake-ups; monitor a condition; read notifications
tools.artifact: publish an HTML page as a private claude.ai artifact; read and answer its comments and its small data store
tools.send_user_file: send a file from the session to the user
tools.push_notification: send a push notification to the user
tools.mcp_resources: list and read resources of the connected MCP servers
tools.github: GitHub connector (the user's account): get_file_contents, create_pull_request, list_issues, issue_write, search_code, pull_request_read, actions_list, get_job_logs, create_branch, push_files
tools.notion: Notion connector (the user's workspace): notion-search, notion-fetch, notion-create-pages, notion-update-page, notion-create-database
tools.google_drive: Google Drive connector (the user's drive): search_files, read_file_content, create_file, update_file, share_file
tools.jam: Jam connector (bug-report recordings): search, getDetails, getConsoleLogs, getNetworkRequests, analyzeVideo
tools.mem: Mem connector (the user's notes): create_note, search_notes, get_note, update_note
tools.bigdata_com: Bigdata.com connector (financial data and documents): bigdata_company_tearsheet, bigdata_search, find_securities, bigdata_fetch_document
tools.etoro: eToro connector (the user's trading account): get-my-portfolio-summary, get-instruments-overview, prepare-trade
tools.claude_docs: Claude Docs connector (living documents on claude.ai): create, read, batch, update, export

rubric.F1: no invented Tool (every Tool corresponds to an instruction)
rubric.F3: the Goal states the document's deliverable
rubric.F4: no invented ordering (every protocol order is stated or implied by the document)
rubric.F5: bindings plausible (each `via` names a runtime tool that can perform the Tool)
